title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: The Ars Technica review
gist: macOS 27 Golden Gate makes Apple Intelligence a mandatory, undeletable system component — consuming up to 22.42GB on M3-class Macs during what the reviewer calls a historic RAM and storage shortage — while dropping Intel Mac support entirely and ending Rosetta 2 for general apps after this release. Apple's top-tier AFM 3 Cloud Pro model runs on Nvidia GPUs inside Google's cloud, Apple Intelligence usage limits with paid overages are explicitly coming, and Golden Gate simultaneously walks back the most-criticized parts of last year's Liquid Glass redesign.

insights.claim: macOS 27 Golden Gate removes the toggle that let users disable Apple Intelligence and delete its multi-gigabyte on-device models, converting generative AI from an optional download into a mandatory system component on every supported Mac.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Forced installation guarantees a 100 percent addressable base for Apple's AI APIs and any future paid tiers — the precondition for monetizing Apple Intelligence.
insights.quote: There used to be a toggle you could hit if you wanted to turn off Apple Intelligence and delete the gigabytes’ worth of AI models it would download to your disk, and now there isn’t.
insights.locator: Generative AI is unavoidable if you install macOS 27

insights.claim: On an M1 MacBook Air, upgrading from Tahoe with Apple Intelligence off to Golden Gate consumes about 17GB more disk space, versus only about 4GB more if Apple Intelligence was already enabled, because a mandatory language model downloads the first time the Mac connects to the Internet.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A 17GB forced storage hit on entry-level SSDs pushes marginal users toward hardware upgrades or paid iCloud storage — a quiet demand driver for Apple.
insights.quote: If you were running Tahoe with Apple Intelligence turned off, Golden Gate needed a whopping 17GB more space on the M1 MacBook Air
insights.locator: In an apples-to-apples comparison

insights.claim: Apple Intelligence consumes roughly 14GB after a fresh install on an M1 MacBook Air and MacBook Neo but 22.42GB on an M3 MacBook Air that qualifies for the larger AFM 3 Core Advanced model, so newer hardware pays a bigger storage tax.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: On-device model size scales with chip tier, which structurally raises the minimum viable SSD capacity Apple can ship and pressures base-model storage configurations upward.
insights.locator: And if you have a Mac that can run the AFM 3 Core Advanced model

insights.claim: The reviewer argues the forced install is unjustified because Golden Gate demonstrably works normally without Apple Intelligence — a Mac kept offline, or macOS run in a virtual machine, never downloads the models and otherwise behaves like Tahoe.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Because the AI layer is technically separable, regulators or an EU-style carve-out could force an opt-out back, which would immediately shrink the paid-AI funnel.
insights.quote: Apple Intelligence is still fundamentally a fully optional component that is layered over the top of the core macOS experience.
insights.locator: One could be forgiven for being upset

insights.claim: Apple still has not committed to shipping Apple Intelligence updates in the EU, so Macs there are expected to behave like the offline case — with the old Spotlight and Siri designs and no AI models installed.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A persistent EU feature gap means Apple is maintaining two macOS experiences, and EU users are a natural addressable market for third-party AI assistants on Mac.
insights.quote: This is presumably how Macs in the EU will behave, since Apple still hasn’t committed to shipping the Apple Intelligence updates there yet.
insights.locator: This is presumably how Macs in the EU

themes.theme: Apple's model stack and its outside dependencies

insights.claim: Apple's baseline on-device model AFM 3 Core was built 'in collaboration with Google,' an unusual public acknowledgment that Apple's foundational on-device AI is not entirely in-house.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Google is now embedded in Apple's on-device AI stack as well as its search default — deepening a dependency that is already an antitrust focal point.
insights.quote: Apple Intelligence in Golden Gate is powered by its AFM 3 Core model, which has been built “in collaboration with Google.”
insights.locator: Apple Intelligence requirements

insights.claim: Apple's top-tier AFM 3 Cloud Pro model for agentic tool use and complex reasoning runs on Nvidia GPUs inside Google's cloud rather than on Apple Silicon servers, with Apple claiming it layers Nvidia, Intel and Google technologies to approximate its own privacy guarantees.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's silicon self-sufficiency story breaks at the frontier tier — it is a Google Cloud and Nvidia customer for the hardest workloads, a real incremental demand line for both.
insights.quote: Apple had to turn to Nvidia GPUs running in Google’s cloud to make this model work
insights.locator: And then there’s AFM 3 Cloud Pro

insights.claim: Despite Apple's marketing emphasis on on-device processing, all the headline Apple Intelligence features — Siri, Image Playground and the Xcode coding assistants — lean heavily on cloud compute, and most Siri queries fail outright with the Internet disconnected.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's AI cost curve is a server-inference cost curve, not a free on-device one — which is precisely why usage limits and fees are coming.
insights.quote: But all the headlining features, including Siri, Image Playgrounds, and the Xcode coding assistants, are leaning heavily on cloud compute to work.
insights.locator: Apple likes to brag about the amount

insights.claim: In Apple's own human-evaluation data for English text generation, evaluators preferred the new AFM 3 Core only 38 percent of the time versus 23 percent for last year's model with 39 percent seeing no difference — meaning nearly a quarter of the time the new on-device model was perceived as a downgrade.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Small on-device models are still inconsistent generation-over-generation; treat vendor claims of on-device model improvement with the same skepticism as benchmark marketing.
insights.quote: evaluators preferred AFM 3 Core 38 percent of the time and last year’s AFM model 23 percent of the time, and they couldn’t tell a difference 39 percent of the time
insights.locator: When it comes to generating English-language text

insights.claim: Apple gets AFM 3 Core Advanced running locally by keeping part of the model in RAM while periodically augmenting it with 'experts' stored on the device's slower SSD, a memory-versus-storage tradeoff that explains the 12GB RAM floor.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: SSD-resident mixture-of-experts makes fast local storage an AI-performance component, strengthening the case that device NAND demand scales with on-device AI.
insights.locator: Apple’s announcement goes into more depth

insights.claim: The AFM 3 Core Advanced model requires an M3-family chip or newer plus at least 12GB of RAM — a configuration no Apple Silicon Mac has ever shipped — which the reviewer reads as a hint that a MacBook Neo with an A19 Pro and 12GB of RAM may appear during Golden Gate's lifespan.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Software requirements leaking unreleased hardware specs is a reliable pre-announcement signal; a 12GB A19 Pro Mac would reset the entry-level Mac price and memory tier.
insights.quote: The RAM requirement is a bit odd—no Apple Silicon Mac has shipped with 12GB of RAM
insights.locator: Apple Intelligence requirements

insights.claim: Apple has confirmed that Apple Intelligence usage limits are coming 'in the future' — covering Siri AI, AI photo editing tools including Clean Up, Extend and Spatial Reframing, Image Playground, Shortcuts cloud-model calls and third-party apps — and that additional usage 'will be available for a fee.'
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: This is the explicit path from free AI features to a consumer AI revenue line inside Apple Services; the trigger is server cost, and the launch release deliberately has no limits.
insights.quote: Apple hasn’t said what limits users can expect, just that they will vary “by feature, request complexity, system demand, system policies, and other factors” and that additional usage “will be available for a fee.”
insights.locator: “Usage limits may apply”

insights.claim: Cloud-model rate limits are tied to the user's Apple ID and shared across apps, so exhausting image credits in Image Playground also exhausts them in any third-party app calling the same model through Apple's APIs.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A per-user shared quota makes third-party developers compete for the same consumer allowance, pushing serious apps back to their own paid model APIs.
insights.quote: That means if you run out of image credits for AFM 3 Cloud (Image) in Image Playground, you’ll be out of credits for any third-party app that calls that model through Apple’s APIs.
insights.locator: Apple allows app developers to access all of these models

insights.claim: The reviewer expects Apple Intelligence limits to be tied to iCloud+ upsells, noting Apple already gates Home app features like camera video summaries behind upper-tier iCloud+ plans.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Bundling AI overages into iCloud+ tiers would raise Services ARPU without a standalone AI subscription SKU — watch for iCloud+ tier repricing.
insights.quote: I wouldn’t be surprised to see other Apple Intelligence limits tied to iCloud upsells
insights.locator: Apple gates some Home app features

insights.claim: On-device Apple models are available to developers without any usage limits while cloud models are rate-limited, creating a structural incentive for third-party apps to design around smaller local models.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Free local inference versus metered cloud inference is the pricing signal that will shape which Mac app features get built on-device.
insights.quote: The on-device models are available to use without any limitations.
insights.locator: Apple allows app developers to access all of these models

themes.theme: End of Intel and the hardware refresh forcing function

insights.claim: Golden Gate is the first macOS release since the mid-2000s that runs on no Intel Macs at all, requiring an M1 chip or newer six years into the Apple Silicon era and dropping the last 2019 and 2020-era Intel machines that ran Tahoe.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A hard cutoff converts a large installed base into forced upgraders over the next two years, supporting Mac unit volumes independent of macro demand.
insights.quote: The Golden Gate update is the first macOS release since the mid-2000s not to run on any Intel Macs.
insights.locator: System requirements: Farewell to Intel

insights.claim: Golden Gate is the last macOS release to offer Rosetta 2 for general-purpose apps; in macOS 28 the x86-to-Arm translation layer will survive only for older games with Intel-specific dependencies.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A one-year deadline for every remaining x86-only Mac app forces vendor recompiles or abandonment — an enterprise software-migration cost landing in 2027.
insights.quote: But this is the last macOS release that will offer Rosetta 2 for general-purpose apps.
insights.locator: Under the hood: Rosetta’s long goodbye

insights.claim: The reviewer recommends anyone with a Mac too old for macOS 15 Sequoia buy new hardware specifically because of how awful pricing has gotten thanks to an ongoing RAM and storage crisis — implying prices will keep rising rather than fall.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A respected reviewer telling readers to buy now ahead of further memory price inflation corroborates a tightening DRAM/NAND cycle affecting consumer device pricing.
insights.quote: My recommendation, due to how awful pricing has gotten thanks to the ongoing RAM and storage crisis, is that anyone with a Mac too old to run macOS 15 Sequoia should very strongly consider a hardware upgrade.
insights.locator: What to do with an unsupported Mac

insights.claim: The escape hatches for stranded Intel Macs are all degrading: OpenCore Legacy Patcher has foundered with its last official update nearly a year ago and never supported Tahoe or the T2 chip, Boot Camp Windows 10 security updates are drying up, and Linux support for T2-based I/O functions is hit or miss.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: With no viable workaround, the Intel Mac base converts to replacement demand rather than extended life — a cleaner upgrade cycle than past transitions.
insights.locator: At one point, running newer versions of macOS

insights.claim: The reviewer flags that some of the Intel Macs now losing major OS updates were being sold as recently as 2023, a notably short major-update support window for machines bought new.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Three-year major-OS support on premium hardware is a reputational and possibly regulatory exposure in markets tightening device-longevity rules.
insights.quote: End of the line for Intel Macs, at least when it comes to major OS updates. Some of these models were being sold as recently as 2023.
insights.locator: The bad

themes.theme: Liquid Glass walkback and developer whiplash

insights.claim: Golden Gate adds a Liquid Glass intensity slider in the device setup flow that ranges from maximum glassiness to a tint level close to the old Big Sur styling, replacing the binary Clear/Tinted toggle Apple introduced in 26.1.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple shipping a user-tunable dial for its own flagship design language is an admission the redesign overshot — a pattern worth watching in iOS and visionOS too.
insights.locator: Choose your glass

insights.claim: The reviewer states that reports of users holding off on OS upgrades because of the Liquid Glass makeover 'turned out to be based on flawed assumptions,' contradicting the popular narrative that the redesign suppressed adoption.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Design controversy in enthusiast circles did not measurably slow OS adoption — a reminder that vocal developer sentiment is a poor proxy for consumer behavior.
insights.quote: Reports that users were holding off on operating system upgrades because of the Liquid Glass makeover turned out to be based on flawed assumptions.
insights.locator: Liquid Glass, take two

insights.claim: Apple reversed course on menu item glyphs one year after pushing them — its Human Interface Guidelines now say icons should be used 'sparingly and with purpose,' penalizing exactly the third-party developers who did the work to follow the prior year's guidance.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Annual reversals raise the real cost of tracking Apple's design guidance, a tax on small Mac developers and an argument for cross-platform UI frameworks.
insights.quote: the losers are third-party app developers that went to the effort to follow last year’s guidelines
insights.locator: However Apple is feeling about menu item glyphs

themes.theme: Siri, vibe coding and the limits of agency

insights.claim: Siri AI is in beta in the US for English speakers only and unavailable elsewhere for a combination of technological and regulatory reasons, while taking over the entire Spotlight interface where it is enabled.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A US-English-only flagship AI feature means Apple's AI differentiation is absent from most of its installed base for at least another cycle.
insights.locator: Siri AI (in beta in the US for English speakers

insights.claim: The reviewer judges the new Siri experience to be so similar to Copilot or Google Search AI answers that it 'barely seems worth remarking upon,' simultaneously showing how far behind Apple was and how quickly it caught up once it shipped something usable.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Chatbot assistants have commoditized to parity, which shifts the competitive battleground from model quality to distribution — where Apple's installed base wins.
insights.quote: like Copilot or the AI answers in Google Search that it barely seems worth remarking upon
insights.locator: By default, Siri uses the Apple models

insights.claim: Siri can toggle Control Center-level settings like Bluetooth, dark mode and brightness but refuses to manipulate advanced system settings or files directly — asking for an image's EXIF data returns instructions rather than the data, and Finder file manipulation is out of scope.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple has deliberately not shipped a true OS agent; the gap between assistant and agent is the space third-party automation tools still own on the Mac.
insights.locator: One consistent barrier is that Siri can only occasionally help

insights.claim: Safari 27's Describe an Extension lets users generate simple browser extensions from plain-language descriptions in a couple of minutes, but it reliably fails whenever the extension must interface with external software or services, and offers no history or undo for iterations.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Consumer vibe coding is capped at self-contained page manipulation; the integration layer remains the moat for real developer tools.
insights.quote: Every time I tried to make an extension that interfaced directly with external software or services in some way, I got an error message
insights.locator: In my own testing, I encountered three broad categories

insights.claim: Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts can only assemble workflows from the pre-set actions apps expose and will not color outside those lines, so an attempt to automate new-Mac setup with app downloads and system tweaks failed almost instantly.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: AI automation on macOS is bounded by the app-exposed action surface, which means platform automation value accrues to whoever controls those action catalogs.
insights.locator: But as with Describe an Extension

insights.claim: Image Playground's ADM 3 Cloud model still drifts through iterations, changing things the user did not ask to change, and the reviewer was able to iterate around copyright guardrails step by step to reach identifiable likenesses the app would refuse to generate in a single prompt.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Single-prompt content filters are trivially defeated by incremental iteration — a live copyright and safety exposure for any consumer image generator.
insights.quote: But I could often iterate to an identifiable likeness of a copyrighted character in a way the app would refuse to do if I tried it all at once.
insights.locator: Apple obviously has some kind of guardrails in place

insights.claim: Safari 27's Notify Me feature monitors specific pages for updates such as price changes, restocks or preorders on an hourly-to-monthly schedule and works even when Safari is closed, though its once-per-hour maximum refresh makes it uncompetitive with dedicated stock-tracker sites and Discord instances for high-demand items.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is absorbing a slice of the price-tracking and restock-alert app category into the browser, squeezing small utilities without killing the scalper-tier tools.
insights.locator: Notify Me

insights.claim: Apple has built its own container tool for Open Container Initiative images as an in-house alternative to Docker and Podman, though it lacks any Docker Desktop GUI equivalent and has no first-party Docker Compose replacement.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A free OS-bundled container runtime erodes the paid Docker Desktop seat base on Mac developer machines, the segment Docker monetizes hardest.
insights.quote: Apart from supporting full-fat VMs, Apple has created
insights.locator: Containers

insights.claim: Golden Gate's Virtualization framework adds VM account provisioning that skips setup, flexible vmnet virtual networks with DHCP and port forwarding, and Accessory Access USB passthrough — features that bring the free built-in framework closer to commercial software like Parallels.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is repeatedly absorbing paid virtualization features into the OS, compressing the value proposition of third-party Mac VM vendors.
insights.locator: Virtualization

insights.claim: DiskImageKit introduces stacked disk images with a read-only base layer, an optional cache layer for fast local storage, and overlay layers recording changes, so many VMs can share one base macOS install while each writes only its own sparse deltas.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Copy-on-write VM layering is the storage-efficiency primitive that makes Mac CI fleets and headless macOS build farms materially cheaper to run.
insights.locator: DiskImageKit

insights.claim: Golden Gate fully removes Apple Filing Protocol support and with it the ability to back up to any surviving Time Capsule, completing a deprecation that began when Big Sur blocked AFP hosting in 2020 and Sequoia 15.5 formally deprecated it.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's removal cadence runs roughly a decade from default-switch to removal — a usable planning constant for anyone depending on a deprecated Apple technology.
insights.locator: Deprecations and removals: AFP and Time Capsule backups

insights.claim: XProtect in Golden Gate may now restrict access to app data commonly targeted by malware, applying App Store sandbox-style folder protections to Discord, Google Chrome, Brave, Microsoft Edge, Firefox, and the crypto wallets Ledger Live, Exodus and Wasabi.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple singling out three crypto wallets for OS-level data protection confirms wallet-file theft is now a mainstream macOS malware objective — relevant to self-custody risk and wallet-vendor security roadmaps.
insights.quote: the list of apps that merit this treatment include Discord, Google Chrome, Brave, Microsoft Edge, Firefox, Ledger Live, Exodus, and Wasabi
insights.locator: Extra protection (and restrictions) for certain apps

insights.claim: An iPad running iPadOS 27 used as a Mac monitor in Sidecar mode now supports direct touchscreen input and Apple has added pull-to-refresh for Mac apps, which the reviewer calls the clearest external sign yet that Apple is preparing touchscreen Macs after years of calling the idea ludicrous.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Touch-input plumbing landing in macOS before the hardware is the standard Apple pre-announcement pattern; a touchscreen Mac would reset display and digitizer supply chains.
insights.quote: they’re our clearest external sign that Apple is preparing
insights.locator: If you have an iPad running iPadOS 27

insights.claim: iPhone Mirroring windows can now be resized dynamically while apps run, with macOS remembering per-app sizes, and the reviewer notes apps updated to work with the iPhone Duo's foldable display should benefit — a direct reference to an Apple foldable phone.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: macOS features being built around a foldable iPhone's multi-column layouts is corroborating evidence that the device is real and near, with foldable-display supply-chain implications.
insights.locator: Right now, core Apple apps like Safari and Mail

insights.claim: Golden Gate adds native support for ultrawide monitors up to 5K resolution at 120 Hz and is the first macOS release to extend HDR to the operating system's own user interface rather than just to content playback.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Closing the ultrawide and HDR-UI gaps removes reasons Mac buyers avoided third-party displays, expanding the addressable market for high-end non-Apple monitors.
insights.locator: Display support: Ultrawides, HDR, and touchscreen breadcrumbs

insights.claim: A future Golden Gate software update will let the Passwords app automatically sign into accounts with weak or compromised passwords and replace them with stronger generated ones, extending beyond today's flagging of reused and breached credentials.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Automated credential rotation baked into the OS is a direct threat to standalone password-manager differentiation on Apple platforms.
insights.locator: Passwords (coming soon)

insights.claim: Apple is not backporting Safari 27's headline features — automatic tab grouping, Notify Me and Describe an Extension — to macOS 15 Sequoia or macOS 26 Tahoe, even though those versions get the same security fixes and WebKit enhancements.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Feature withholding on supported older OSes is the soft lever Apple uses to drive upgrades when hardware cutoffs alone are not enough.
insights.locator: Safari 27 for macOS 15 Sequoia and macOS 26 Tahoe
